title: Mammillaria geminispina
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of cactus}} {{Speciesbox | image = Mammillaria geminispina 2.jpg | image_caption = M. geminispina | image2 = Cactus2.jpg | image2_caption = Patch of M. geminispina, with examples of crested mutations. | status = LC | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Gómez-Hinostrosa, C. |author2=Sánchez , E. |author3=Guadalupe Martínez, J. |author4=Bárcenas Luna, R. |year=2017 |amends=2013 |title=''Mammillaria geminispina'' |volume=2017 |article-number=e.T151876A121511748 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2017-3.RLTS.T151876A121511748.en |language=en |access-date=29 April 2026}} | genus = Mammillaria | species = geminispina | authority = [[Adrian Hardy Haworth|Haw.]] }} '''''Mammillaria geminispina''''', the '''twin spined cactus''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Cactaceae, [[native plant|native]] to central Mexico. == Description == The growth habit of ''M. geminispina'' is variable; most grow into clump-forming colonies, though some are solitary specimens, while others still have only very few offsets. The species matures with long, white spines at the end of conical [[tubercle]]s, distinct among the ''Mammillaria''. Between these tubercles is white wool. Foliage tissue is a teal-blue to dark seafoam-green.{{Cite web |title=''Mammillaria geminispina'' |url=http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/CACTI/Family/Cactaceae/14012/Mammillaria_geminispina |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=llifle.com}} == Flowers == Carmine-pink flowers are borne in a crown formation around the head of the plant, with blooming occurring in summer and autumn. Flowers are [[Pollination|pollinated]] and develop into small, ovate fruits, which are technically edible and have a tart, fruity flavor. These fruits are consumed by birds, rodents and some reptiles, which aid in spreading the species' seed to new locations.{{cite book |title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants |publisher=Dorling Kindersley |year=2008 |isbn=978-1405332965 |location=United Kingdom |pages=1136}} ==Cultivation== ''Mammillaria geminispina'' is one of several ''Mammillaria'' species to be cultivated.{{cite web|title=Cactus Art - ''Mammillaria geminispina''|url=http://www.cactus-art.biz/schede/MAMMILLARIA/Mammillaria_geminispina/Mammillaria_geminispina/mammillaria_geminispina.htm|access-date=26 June 2013}} It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Mammillaria geminispina''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/106178/Mammillaria-geminispina/Details | access-date = 29 October 2020}}{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 63 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 March 2018}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q148155}} [[Category:Mammillaria|geminispina]] [[Category:Cacti of Mexico]] [[Category:Endemic flora of Mexico]] [[Category:Flora of Hidalgo (state)]] [[Category:Flora of Querétaro]] [[Category:Flora of San Luis Potosí]]
